  • The package documents a csr CLI. Ordinary console_scripts/CLI behavior requires user invocation and is not treated as malicious automatic execution evidence.

Theft/Exfiltration/Persistence/Lateral Movement/Obfuscation

  • **Credential harvesting:** Not confirmed. csr.py reads VS Code/GitHub Copilot session stores such as workspaceStorage, state.vscdb, and chatSessions/*.jsonl, but this matches the documented purpose of a local session-recall CLI. The provided corpus does not show broad discovery of .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, or similar secrets.
  • **Exfiltration/staging:** Not confirmed. zlib/gzip usage appears to decode VS Code blob/JSON data. There is no evidence of archive staging, temporary collection for upload, webhook use, or external C2 transmission.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile modification, background polling, or similar persistence.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket access, cloud metadata use, GitHub Actions/CI token use, or workflow injection.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** zlib.decompress, gzip.decompress, and regular expressions were flagged, but they are not paired with eval/exec, dynamic code execution, downloader behavior, or encrypted payload loading. Based on the available evidence, they do not indicate a malicious loader.

  • The manifest lists 10 files, mainly csr.py, README/PKG-INFO, egg-info metadata, pyproject.toml, and setup.cfg.
  • No evidence was provided for unexpected native binaries, hidden payloads, typosquatting, suspicious dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch.
